king

course: The course sets a basic foundation of fiction and narrative, I genuinely learned and internalised the texts we covered. But, the reading assignments sometimes made me feel overwhelmed, as I needed to read other texts from other 2 Elit courses at the same time.

I wish we could have studied more theoretical texts. I think a course titled “Fiction and Narrative” offers a great opportunity for that. The theoretical texts we did study in class were very enlightening, and the instructor was very effective at teaching those topics as well.
It felt like a long case study. I believe that there could have been more theory/general information balanced with the works we read and analysed.

instructor: I think he's at his best/most interesting when discussing topics that are only tangentially related to the main subject. I like his subtle allusions to philosophy (wish he would expand on the intertextual side of the course more). Tim Hoca clearly loves his job. You can say that from the first lesson. He is a nice person who wants to teach his students. He is very kind about helping the students.
course: well chosen texts. the course really helps students to understand the novels in a critical way.

the chosen texts are not engaging at all - makes the entire course painfully dull (when fiction and narrative by itself is an exciting topic). ideally, should direct much more attention towards subtopics and intertextuality, rather than attempting to analyze entire novels at once.

instructor: After taking multiple courses from Tim, I can say with absolute certainty that he is the best instructor I’ve ever had. In every sense. His level of intellect, humour and empathy is truly unmatched. He is so open to new ideas that the students bring and doesn’t dismiss any interpretations in class discussions. He does not get mad at students, not even slightly, for not reading the assigned parts, which I find quite remarkable. He is respectful and very understanding. Also, he gives the context of the reading materials to ensure we comprehend them correctly. He even did a little presentation to make us fully understand the setting of one book we had. He is careful about those little details. He focuses on really interesting parts of our readings, so you don't get bored in class. He clearly says what he expects from you on the assignments. His comments and feedback on assignments are also helpful. I think that his grading is fair. The readings he chose were also incredibly enjoyable. I don’t remember having this much fun from any other ELIT elective. Honestly, I can’t think of anything negative about Tim. A great person in general. What a warm, gentle soul. He truly is one of a kind. I feel so lucky to have taken classes from him.
He has no weakest points. A very understanding person and great instructor. He is also funny.
He is perfect.
One of the greatest this faculty has to offer.
course: I loved the readings! I like the fact that they were very diverse in every aspect. The course syllabus did have some very interesting works. Zoo City especially, felt like a fresh breath. Great focus on female writers, which is also something that I really appreciated.
By far the strangest books I read this year.

instructor: He is a brilliant teacher. I enjoyed his teaching style as well as the readings we did. I'm glad I took this class.

instructor: creative and dedicative

He is really good at making classes interesting. His teaching skills are admirable, plus he is always nice and respectful to his students. The fact that I like the most about him is his sincere attitude towards his students. You can clearly see he is not trying to make things harder for students.

He really wants too much without giving anything. He does not state exactly what he wants, I don't think his grading is absolutely fair. If you want to say something, you have to wait for the always speaking people to be silent, and then talk if there is enough time. In short, he is struggling with how I can downgrade the student's grade. In the online period, it was very tiring for the whole class that this lesson very challenging by the teacher became among all the chaos that we live. Although it was an elective course, it was exhausting from all my department courses and it affected psychologically. If he doesn't like you, you can't get high grade no matter what you do. All your efforts are wasted. Even if you try to attend classes to get a high grade in an unfair environment, it is impossible to get a high grade from Timothy without having excellent English and super confidence.

course: I think this may be the best course I have taken in Elit department (and I am a senior). Almost every 2 weeks the literary works we read changed. All of the books were about different cities, it helps us to learn about different cultures and how literature functions in different places. The course is almost like a mini-world-tour. One week you are in London, one week in Delhi, one in Paris... I hope the course will continue to be given in the future semesters.

This course cannot be an elective course, it is very difficult for an elective. The instructor even made it harder for students. The readings were too much, the expectations were merciless and unfair. There are lots of difficult quizzes and 2 midterms 1 final. In such a difficult semester psychologically, mentally, and physiologically, the instructor was never understanding and helpful for the students. Making a pop quiz in the last week of the semester and laughing at this not makes you a good instructor, it shows how abnormal and bad-hearted you are as a teacher even a person actually.

I also think his questions for our exams were a bit repetitive and strange.  But he gave us a lot of freedom to play around with them, which was nice. On a positive side, you can tell he loves what he does. He really seems to enjoy hearing our opinions and discussing his own ideas with us. This makes it easier to communicate with him.
He is very respectable and polite.

He handled the situation of pandemic very well. I didn't have any issues regarding learning. In fact, I was able to communicate better. He also adjusted our essays for the pandemic too so I'm very grateful for that. I did not have any problems regarding assignments and quizzes. instructor: I do not believe he is really a good instructor. He only speaks with his favorite students, he lets them speak more than enough. His grading is not fair and quite low. He gives feedback saying ok good, interesting, and etc., and then you end with a very low, unexpected grade. I have no idea about his aims, as they are weird and hard to interpret. I am feeling so regretful that I take the class from him. I am really bored with unfair instructors and the system! The quizzes were too much and making the quizzes at the very beginning of the class and giving 15 minutes to complete them, is never ever fair nor logical! There might be students who have a really bad internet connection or have any other issues related to their house or family, so the instructor should take these important issues into consideration, please. There are students who have social anxieties or do not have very well speaking English, so please do not expect us to participate in all of your discussions! And just because we did not participate in a discussion, do not give us a lower participation grade. We are grown-up people like you, and we need those grades, it is not an easy thing for us to go abroad and find a job, even though it may be for you! Our country sadly is not a very successful place to find a job, especially you are studying ELIT! Thank you.

course: Putting 2 midterms and a 1 final, you only create more stress and pressure on us. Every department made only 1 midterm and 1 final exam, and guess what our department the ELIT department made 2 midterms! We are also humans, we need some time to refresh and feel like a normal human being and spend some time with our family and with ourselves. When I told this fact to other class instructors they also get shocked by this unlogical and meaningless system. Both the school and the instructors made students feel insufficient, incompetent, unsuccessful, and stressed, whereas you should have made our job easier in this harsh and horrible time, seeing many people dying every second day in the news, is not something to feel motivated for us to write lots of essays and be perfect. Expecting us to be perfect and do the readings on time is never logical and will never ever be logical in the upcoming semesters as well!
